newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Tiger cub dies at Dhaka zoo after mother's death.
newsitem.headline: Tiger cub dies at Dhaka zoo after mother's death.

text.p: A baby tiger has died at Bangladesh's national zoo, only days after its mother and two other rare Bengal tigers died of suspected poisoning, zoo officials said on Thursday.

"The three-month-old male cub, breast-fed until his mother's death on Monday, suffered a fatal intestinal obstruction after it was given meat," a zoo doctor, who declined to be named, said. He said the cub died on Wednesday.
"It was the first time he ate meat and he just couldn't stand it," the zoo doctor told Reuters, adding that another cub was suffering a similar illness.
Dr. Nazrul Islam of the government's directorate of livestocks said: "We have stopped giving them (the cubs) meat and are now trying to feed them with cow's milk in bottles."
The cub's mother was one of three Bengal tigers which died during the past week.
Zoo authorities told reporters they suspected the three had been poisoned, but added this could not be confirmed until laboratory tests were finished.
The government has ordered an inquiry into the deaths.

Besides 16 tigers left in the national zoo, Bangladesh has only some 400 Bengal tigers left in the coastal Sundarban forests, nearly 400 km (250 miles) south of Dhaka, according to official estimates.
